free_tier.notes: No numeric rate limit is published. The documented guidance is 'back off if you start seeing 429 statuses'.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: paged JSON. rows=1000 with a select list returned 773,304 bytes in one response here.

retention.stated: the registry only grows; records are corrected rather than deleted, and the API is the live view

egress.terms: Free and unmetered. No key, no account, no allowance published.

interface_detail: GET https://api.crossref.org/works with rows, cursor and select; content negotiation for single records. The polite pool is signalled with mailto= or a User-Agent carrying an address.
tooling: curl/python-requests; the harvester package and the documented cursor pattern. No SDK required.
chaining: Crossref supplies the DOI-level citation graph and licence metadata; the full text behind each DOI is a separate fetch from the publisher or from an OA mirror such as PMC or Europe PMC.

limits.value: no number published; the tips page says 'pay attention to the http status code and back off if you start seeing 429 statuses'
cursor paging is required past the first page; rows=1000 is accepted and returned 773,304 bytes here

limits_note: The documented bulk snapshot did not work: https://api.crossref.org/snapshots/monthly/latest.json.gz answered 200 with 41 bytes of text/html and no body, and /snapshots answered 200 with a zero-byte body. That is a false-200 shape, not a file.
binding_note: At 773 KB per rows=1000 call, 1 TiB is about 1.4 million calls; the call rate, which is unpublished and signalled only by 429, is what decides the day's bytes.

identity_cost.detail: No sign-up is required. A mailto in the query or User-Agent is a courtesy that routes the caller to the polite pool; it is not a credential.

reliability_note: The polite pool is the difference between a fast run and a 429 storm, and it costs only an email in the User-Agent; the snapshot endpoint is silently broken and returns a 200 stub, which a naive client will save as a data file.
confidence_note: Two endpoints were exercised with byte counts and the vendor page was read. No 429 was triggered here, so the unpublished rate ceiling is not characterised.

evidence.proved: 'No sign-up is required to use the REST API' and the polite-pool mailto pattern
'back off if you start seeing 429 statuses' - the only published rate signal; cursor paging for bulk
200, 773,304 bytes of application/json in 3,456 ms - the real bytes per call
200 with 41 bytes of text/html and no file - the documented snapshot URL did not serve a snapshot
